newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.1 pct Sept - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.1 pct Sept - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales fell 0.1 percent in the first two weeks of fiscal September versus August, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 5.1 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 4.9 percent in the week ended September 14 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

The pace of sales growth continued to run below expectations, although certain stores last week may have been negatively affected by mismatched comparisons with last year's Labor Day, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst of Redbook Research.

"The comparison against Labor Day a year ago generated some good volume ... and (retailers) were up against those numbers - that may have pulled the figures down," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Looking at the impact of poor weather on the southern East Coast, Eilenberg said he didn't see any rebound from the hurricane-related areas, "so business was kind of weak last week."
Eilenberg also said tough comparisons against September a year ago may have contributed to the slight decline in sales.
"Retailers did not have very ambitious plans for the month of September, they are more optimistic for October, November and December," added Eilenberg.
